_schema: Composite signal weights (docs/006_Scoring_System.md). This file is version-controlled: every weight change is a reviewed commit with its evidence, never an automatic update (human oversight invariant). The composite engine loads these over its built-in defaults.

findings: inventory_surprise: Spearman IC +0.131 at 1w — predictive in both sample halves (+0.203 / +0.061)
price_momentum_5d: IC +0.006 overall with sign flip across halves (+0.103 / -0.075) — drift detected, not predictive standalone
raw IC-proportional split would be 96/4; moderated to 76/24 of the shared 0.34 budget because momentum retains value as a staleness-aware fast-tape check even without standalone alpha

chokepoint_capacity.why: Introduced 2026-07-26 after a documented failure: geopolitical_risk sat pinned at 100/100 for three weeks (rhetoric) while ~8.5M bbl/day still transited the strait and US crude inventories BUILT +2.0M bbl. Event severity and realized supply impact diverged, and the composite had no way to see it.
chokepoint_capacity.weight_basis: Taken FROM geopolitical_risk (0.30 -> 0.18 + 0.12), not added on top. Both measure the same underlying phenomenon — supply disruption — so the 'disruption budget' stays at 0.30 total, with 40% of it routed through the harder, physically-measured input rather than the narrative one.
chokepoint_capacity.honest_limitation: There is no information coefficient for this component. The observation series began 2026-07-17 and has too few points for any IC to mean anything. The 0.12 is reasoned, not measured. Revisit once >=26 weekly observations exist and the backtest engine can score it; if it fails to add predictive value, cut it back to geopolitical_risk.

changelog.note: Split the disruption budget: geopolitical_risk 0.30→0.18, new chokepoint_capacity 0.12 (realized shipping capacity). Total unchanged at 0.30. Provisional and un-backtested — see provisional_weights.
